issues.legal_issue: An alleged oral agreement to reconvey property must be proved by convincing evidence before specific performance can be granted.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought specific performance of an alleged oral agreement to reconvey property sold under a written deed.
The deed recorded an outright transfer and contained only a restriction on mortgaging or assigning the property during the vendor’s lifetime; it did not record an agreement to reconvey.
The plaintiff gave no satisfactory explanation for not recording the alleged reconveyance agreement in writing.
The principal supporting witnesses were interested or unreliable, and a document relied on to support the agreement was found suspicious.
The trial court itself observed that there was no clear-cut evidence proving the terms of the alleged oral contract.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff failed to prove the alleged agreement, and the claim for specific performance on that basis could not succeed.
issues.legal_principle: The burden of proving the alleged contract rested on the plaintiff. A specific-performance contract must be specific and established by convincing evidence; a decree is rarely granted where the agreement rests solely on oral evidence. The judgment concerns specific performance under section 12 of the Specific Relief Act 1877.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and alleged_reconveyance_was_oral and sale_document_recorded_an_outright_transfer and no_satisfactory_explanation_for_omitting_reconveyance_from_writing and supporting_evidence_was_unconvincing

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The claimant brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.alleged_reconveyance_was_oral: The claimant alleged that the agreement to reconvey the property was made orally.
predicates.sale_document_recorded_an_outright_trans: The written transfer document recorded an outright conveyance and did not record the alleged agreement to reconvey.
predicates.no_satisfactory_explanation_for_omitting: The claimant did not satisfactorily explain why the alleged reconveyance agreement was not recorded in writing.
predicates.supporting_evidence_was_unconvincing: The evidence supporting the alleged agreement was interested, unreliable, suspicious, or otherwise insufficiently convincing.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks specific performance of an alleged oral reconveyance agreement, an outright written transfer, an unexplained omission of the alleged agreement from that writing, and unconvincing supporting evidence mean the agreement is not proved.

issues.legal_issue: A court cannot grant specific performance on the basis of a different agreement pleaded by the defendant when the claimant has not accepted and sought performance of that agreement or pleaded readiness and willingness to perform it.
material_facts: The defendant’s written statement described an agreement to sell part of the property for a specified price, which differed from the oral reconveyance agreement pleaded by the plaintiff.
The plaintiff did not amend the pleadings or otherwise seek relief on the basis of the defendant’s agreement.
The plaintiff did not accept that agreement as true or plead that he was ready and willing to perform it.
The High Court nevertheless ordered a sale on the terms stated in the defendant’s written statement.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was wrong to decree specific performance on the basis of the defendant’s different agreement.
issues.legal_principle: A specific-performance claim must set out the agreement sued upon and plead that the claimant applied for its performance, that the other party failed to perform, and that the claimant has been and remains ready and willing to perform. The judgment relies on Forms 47 and 48 in the First Schedule to the Code of Civil Procedure and applies Pt. Prem Raj v. The D.L.F. Housing and Construction (Private) Ltd. and distinguishes Srinivas Ram Kumar v. Mahabir Prasad.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The claimant brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.defendant_pleaded_a_different_contract: The defendant described a contract materially different from the contract on which the claimant based the suit.
predicates.claimant_did_not_accept_or_seek_relief_o: The claimant neither accepted the defendant’s version of the contract nor amended the claim to seek relief on its basis.
predicates.claimant_did_not_plead_readiness_and_wil: The claimant did not plead readiness and willingness to perform the contract described by the defendant.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance proceeding, a decree cannot rest on the defendant’s different contract when the claimant did not accept or seek relief on it and did not plead readiness and willingness to perform it.

issues.legal_issue: Each side may be directed to bear its own costs when both sides have withheld the true version of events and the defendant later withdraws an offer made in the pleadings.
material_facts: The Court considered it likely that neither side had presented the true account of the transaction.
The sale price was substantially below the property’s value, but the parties had not explained why.
The defendant had stated in the written statement a willingness to sell part of the property for a stated price, but later appeared unwilling to stand by that offer as property values had risen.
issues.conclusion: The parties were directed to bear their own costs throughout.
issues.legal_principle: In the circumstances of this case, the Court considered it appropriate to depart from an award of costs to either side because neither had placed the true version before the Court and the defendant had retreated from the offer made in the written statement.

predicates.civil_litigation: The matter is a civil proceeding in which the Court must determine costs.
predicates.both_sides_withheld_the_true_version: The parties failed to place the true account of the transaction before the Court.
predicates.defendant_later_withdrew_a_pleaded_offer: The defendant later ceased to stand by an offer previously made in the pleadings.

issues.definition: In civil litigation, when both sides withhold the true account and the defendant later withdraws a pleaded offer, each side bears its own costs.
